title: beauty-mvp: Mobile Shopping Demo (Browse, Product Detail, Cart) - Product Requirements Document
summary: beauty-mvp is a simple, attractive Flutter mobile app (iOS and Android) where beauty shoppers browse a sample catalog of about 20-30 products, view clear product details and add items to an in-session cart. The first release is a demo for stakeholders, investors and partners. It proves the core shopping experience before the business invests in full checkout, payments, accounts and a live backend. Scope is limited to three screens: Browse (with category filter), Product Detail and Cart. Product data comes from a bundled local JSON file plus image files supplied by the business. All prices are in USD and all text is in English. The cart lives in memory only and is lost when the app closes. The cart ends at the total, with no checkout entry point, placeholder button, accounts, search, sorting, variants, stock display, promotions, tax, shipping or analytics. Prices are held as integer cents with currency code USD and displayed as dollars, never as floats. The data model is kept easy to extend so the codebase can later grow into a full ecommerce app without a rewrite. Target delivery is roughly 4-6 weeks, in 2 milestones: (1) style proposal approval, catalog loading, Browse and category filter, Product Detail; (2) Cart, polish, accessibility and performance checks, demo build on an iPhone and a mid-range Android phone.

personas.name: Beauty shopper
personas.description: Woman or man aged 18-40 who buys skincare, makeup and haircare products and is comfortable shopping on their phone. Often an existing customer of the online and in-store beauty business.
goals: Quickly browse the catalog and find products in a category of interest
Understand a product clearly (image, brand, price, description, ingredients or usage notes) before adding it to the cart
Collect items in a cart and see an accurate total

personas.name: Existing customer
personas.description: Current customer of the online and in-store beauty business who wants a faster, more convenient way to browse the catalog on a phone.
goals: Browse the familiar catalog more conveniently than on the website or in store
See clear prices and product information
Keep track of items of interest in a cart while using the app

personas.name: Internal stakeholder, investor or partner
personas.description: Person who sees the first demo and judges the quality of the experience and the brand presentation.
goals: See a polished, premium, beauty-oriented app running on both iOS and Android
Walk through browse, detail and cart smoothly without errors or dead ends
Gain confidence that the codebase can grow into a full ecommerce app

user_stories.title: Browse the product catalog
user_stories.i_want: to scroll through a grid of products showing image, name, brand and price
user_stories.so_that: I can quickly see what the brand offers

acceptance_criteria.given: the app is launched and the bundled catalog of 20-30 products loads successfully
acceptance_criteria.when: the Browse screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.then: a scrollable grid shows every product in the All view, and each tile shows the product image, name, brand and price formatted in USD (for example $24.50)

acceptance_criteria.given: the Browse screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: I scroll to the end of the grid
acceptance_criteria.then: all products in the catalog are reachable by scrolling alone, with no search field or sort control present

acceptance_criteria.given: a product image is slow to load or fails to load
acceptance_criteria.when: its tile is displayed
acceptance_criteria.then: a placeholder is shown in the image area, the name, brand and price remain visible, and the app does not crash or block scrolling

acceptance_criteria.given: the catalog file cannot be read or parsed
acceptance_criteria.when: the app launches
acceptance_criteria.then: a friendly error message with a retry action is shown instead of a blank screen or a crash

user_stories.title: Filter products by category
user_stories.i_want: to filter the product grid by Skincare, Makeup, Haircare or Fragrance
user_stories.so_that: I can focus on the type of product I am interested in

acceptance_criteria.given: the Browse screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: I look at the category filter
acceptance_criteria.then: the options All, Skincare, Makeup, Haircare and Fragrance are visible, All is selected by default, and the selected option is clearly highlighted

acceptance_criteria.given: the Browse screen is displayed with All selected
acceptance_criteria.when: I select a category such as Makeup
acceptance_criteria.then: only products whose category is Makeup are shown, and each product appears in exactly one category

acceptance_criteria.given: a category is selected
acceptance_criteria.when: I select All
acceptance_criteria.then: the full catalog is shown again

acceptance_criteria.given: I select a category and open a product then return to Browse
acceptance_criteria.when: the Browse screen is displayed again
acceptance_criteria.then: the previously selected category is still applied

user_stories.title: View product details
user_stories.i_want: to open a product and see a large image, name, brand, price, short description and key ingredients or usage notes
user_stories.so_that: I can decide whether to buy it

acceptance_criteria.given: the Browse screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: I tap a product tile
acceptance_criteria.then: the Product Detail screen opens showing a large product image, name, brand, price in USD, short description, key ingredients or usage notes, a quantity selector and an Add to Cart button

acceptance_criteria.given: the Product Detail screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: I use the back control or the system back gesture
acceptance_criteria.then: I return to the Browse screen at the same scroll position and with the same category filter

acceptance_criteria.given: the Product Detail screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: I look for stock information, variant selectors (shade or size), reviews or wishlist controls
acceptance_criteria.then: none are shown, because every product is a single, always-available purchasable item

user_stories.title: Add a product to the cart with a quantity
user_stories.i_want: to choose a quantity and add the product to my cart
user_stories.so_that: I can collect the items I want

acceptance_criteria.given: the Product Detail screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: it first opens
acceptance_criteria.then: the quantity selector shows 1, the minimum allowed quantity, and the decrease control is disabled at 1

acceptance_criteria.given: the quantity selector shows 10
acceptance_criteria.when: I try to increase it further
acceptance_criteria.then: the quantity stays at 10 and the increase control is disabled, because the maximum per cart line is 10

acceptance_criteria.given: the cart does not contain the product and I have selected a quantity of 3
acceptance_criteria.when: I tap Add to Cart
acceptance_criteria.then: a cart line is created with quantity 3, confirmation feedback is shown, and a cart item count indicator reflects the new total number of units in the cart

acceptance_criteria.given: the cart already contains the product with quantity 8
acceptance_criteria.when: I add 5 more of the same product
acceptance_criteria.then: the existing cart line is updated instead of a duplicate line being created, the quantity is capped at 10, and a message tells me the maximum per line is 10

user_stories.title: View and manage the cart
user_stories.i_want: to see my cart items, change quantities, remove items and see subtotals and an overall total
user_stories.so_that: I know exactly what I have selected and what it costs

acceptance_criteria.given: the cart contains items
acceptance_criteria.when: I open the Cart screen
acceptance_criteria.then: each line shows the product image, name, brand, unit price, quantity and line subtotal (unit price multiplied by quantity), and an overall total equal to the sum of all line subtotals is shown in USD

acceptance_criteria.given: the Cart screen shows a line with quantity 2
acceptance_criteria.when: I increase the quantity to 3
acceptance_criteria.then: the line subtotal and the overall total update immediately, and the quantity cannot go above 10 or below 1 using the quantity controls

acceptance_criteria.given: the Cart screen shows a line
acceptance_criteria.when: I remove the line
acceptance_criteria.then: the line disappears, the overall total and the cart item count indicator update, and the other lines are unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: I remove the last line in the cart
acceptance_criteria.when: the cart becomes empty
acceptance_criteria.then: an empty-cart message with an action to return to Browse is shown and no total is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: the Cart screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: I look at the area below the total
acceptance_criteria.then: there is no checkout, payment, promo code, shipping or tax element, and the screen ends at the total

acceptance_criteria.given: the cart contains items and I navigate between Browse, Product Detail and Cart
acceptance_criteria.when: I return to the Cart screen while the app stays open
acceptance_criteria.then: the cart contents are unchanged; if the app is fully closed and reopened, the cart is empty

user_stories.title: Consistent, branded and accessible look and feel
user_stories.as_a: stakeholder or shopper using an iPhone or an Android phone
user_stories.i_want: a clean, premium, beauty-oriented design with readable text and sufficient contrast on both platforms
user_stories.so_that: the demo reflects the brand quality and is comfortable to use

acceptance_criteria.given: the business has supplied its logo and approved the proposed style (colors, typography, imagery guidelines)
acceptance_criteria.when: I use any of the three screens on iOS and on Android
acceptance_criteria.then: the approved colors, typography and logo are applied consistently and the layout has no overflow or clipping

acceptance_criteria.given: the device text size is increased in the system accessibility settings to 150%
acceptance_criteria.when: I view Browse, Product Detail and Cart
acceptance_criteria.then: product name, price, quantity and the Add to Cart button remain readable and usable without overlapping or being cut off

acceptance_criteria.given: any screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: text and interactive elements are checked against the style
acceptance_criteria.then: body text is at least 14 sp, text/background contrast is at least 4.5:1, interactive controls have a touch target of at least 48x48 dp, and images and controls have accessibility labels for screen readers

non_functional_requirements: Platforms: a single Flutter codebase running on iOS 14 or later and Android 8 (API 26) or later; phones only in portrait; tablets and web are not required. The team may recommend different minimum OS versions, and the client will be informed if so.
Demo devices: the demo is verified on a recent iPhone and a recent mid-range Android phone.

Performance: cold start to a visible Browse screen within 3 seconds on a recent mid-range phone; product grid scrolls smoothly (target 60 fps, no visible jank); product images are sized appropriately for mobile, cached after first load and show a placeholder while loading so they load quickly on typical mobile connections.
Performance: quantity changes, add to cart and remove actions update the UI within 100 ms, since all cart logic is local.

Data: the catalog (about 20-30 products) is loaded from a bundled local JSON file with bundled image files; no live backend, inventory or order system is required. Each product has an ID, name, brand, exactly one category, price, short description, key ingredients or usage notes and an image. The data model is structured so variants and additional fields can be added later without a rewrite.

Money: prices are stored as integer minor units (cents) with ISO 4217 currency code USD, never as floating-point numbers. The display is formatted as USD (for example $24.50), and line subtotals and the total are computed in integer cents with no rounding errors.
Localization: English only and USD only.

Security and privacy: the app collects no personal data, has no accounts or sign-in, and stores nothing on the device beyond the app bundle (the cart is in memory only). No analytics, event tracking or advertising SDKs are included, so no consent flow is needed. No card or payment data is handled.

Accessibility: minimum body text of 14 sp, contrast of at least 4.5:1 for text, touch targets of at least 48x48 dp, screen-reader labels for images and controls, and layouts that remain usable at 150% system text scale.
Reliability: the app does not crash when images fail to load or when the catalog file is missing or malformed; in those cases a placeholder or an error message with retry is shown.
Maintainability: the codebase is structured (separation of UI, state and data) so the local data source can later be replaced by a backend API and checkout can be added without a rewrite.
Testing: acceptance criteria are covered by automated widget tests and at least one integration test of the journey Browse, Filter, Detail, Add to Cart, Cart.
out_of_scope: Checkout, payments, payment providers and any checkout entry point or placeholder button in the cart
User accounts, sign-in, sign-up, profiles and account deletion
Order creation, order status, order history and fulfilment
Guest or signed-in cart persistence across app restarts (the cart is in-session only)
Search and sorting (by price, popularity or anything else)
Product variants (shades, sizes) and per-variant stock tracking
Stock display, out-of-stock states and inventory integration
Promotions, discounts, promo codes, shipping costs and tax estimates
Analytics, event tracking and feedback collection inside the app
Live backend, catalog integration, server-side APIs and Stripe integration
Multiple currencies or languages; regions and shipping rules
Tablet layouts, web and landscape orientation
Push notifications, deep links and social sharing
Legal and privacy requirements such as cosmetics labeling, tax and data privacy flows, to be revisited in a later phase
assumptions: The project conventions for signed-in carts, stock reservation, order status flow, order lines and Stripe payments do not apply to this release, because the client brief and clarifications explicitly exclude accounts, checkout, payments, orders and stock. They will apply when those phases are added.
The demo needs no backend API, so there are no API operations in this release. If the team keeps a stub service for later phases, only the health check endpoint is required.
The business supplies about 20-30 products as a JSON file (or a spreadsheet converted to JSON using a template from the team) plus image files, so the team does not need to source content.
Each product belongs to exactly one of the categories Skincare, Makeup, Haircare and Fragrance; All is a view showing every product and not a category.
Each product is a single always-available item; the quantity per cart line ranges from 1 to 10.
Adding a product already in the cart merges into the existing line, capped at 10 units.
The cart total is a simple sum of line subtotals (price multiplied by quantity) in USD.
The business will supply its logo; the team proposes a simple, premium, beauty-oriented style (colors, typography, imagery) and sends it for approval early in the project.

Delivery targets roughly 4-6 weeks in two milestones: (1) style approval, catalog loading, Browse with category filter, Product Detail; (2) Cart, polish, accessibility and performance checks, demo build.
The app has three main screens (Browse with category filter, Product Detail, Cart), plus an optional simple splash screen that is not counted as a functional screen.
The next phase (checkout and payments, accounts, or backend and catalog integration) is not decided yet and does not affect this release.
